title: Χελιδὼν καὶ κορώνη ⟨περὶ κάλλους φιλονεικοῦσαι⟩
titleEn: The Swallow and the Crow Contending over Beauty
part: The Swallow and the Crow Contending over Beauty (Chambry 348)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 348. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Χελιδὼν καὶ κορώνη περὶ κάλλους ἐφιλονείκουν· ὑποτυχοῦσα δὲ ἡ κορώνη πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· « Ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν σὸν κάλλος τὴν ἐαρινὴν ὥραν ἀνθεῖ, τὸ δὲ ἐμὸν σῶμα καὶ χειμῶνι παρατείνεται. »
sentences.tr: Chelidōn kai korōnē peri kallous ephiloneikoun· hypotychousa de hē korōnē pros autēn eipen· « Alla to men son kallos tēn earinēn hōran anthei, to de emon sōma kai cheimōni parateinetai. »
sentences.l: A swallow and a crow were contending about beauty; and the crow, taking-up-the-word, said to her: « But your beauty blooms for the spring season, while my body is stretched out through the winter too. »
sentences.i: A swallow and a crow were quarrelling over beauty, and the crow took up the word and said to her: « Your beauty flowers for the length of the spring; my body lasts out the winter as well. »
sentences.n: τὴν ἐαρινὴν ὥραν is an accusative of extent of time — the beauty lasts as long as the spring and no longer — while χειμῶνι is the dative of the time within which. ἀνθεῖ is the verb of flowers coming out, used here of the swallow's beauty, which opens and closes with the season. The title carries Chambry's supplement ⟨περὶ κάλλους φιλονεικοῦσαι⟩, 'contending over beauty', which the English title takes in without brackets.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι ἡ τοῦ σώματος παράτασις εὐπρεπείας καλλίων.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hē tou sōmatos paratasis euprepeias kalliōn.
sentences.l: The story shows that the body's lasting is finer than fair looks.
sentences.n: παράτασις is the noun belonging to the crow's παρατείνεται — the stretching out, the holding on. καλλίων takes the genitive of comparison, εὐπρεπείας, with no word for 'than'; the copula is left out, as regularly in a maxim.
